item.title: Awkward Silences: A Tribute to Rabbi Sacks & Why Silence Is a Virtue | Hilchot Deot Ch. 2
item.description:
Why is silence a virtue? Hilchot Deot 2, given the week Rabbi Sacks passed away: speaking little and listening, the prohibition of smooth talk and being two-faced, and Genevat Daat, creating a false impression without a false word, with the Rambam's cases and modern examples.

item.title: Is Self-Denial Holy? Jealousy, Desire & Enjoying This World | Hilchot Deot Ch. 2-3
item.description:
Is self-denial holy? Hilchot Deot 2 and 3: joy as the natural state, contentment with money, how jealousy, desire and honour take a person out of the world, the prohibition of withdrawing through constant fasting or deliberate deprivation, and engaging with the world so that even eating and sleep serve God.

item.title: Rambam's Diet: Why Staying Healthy Is Halacha | Hilchot Deot Ch. 4
item.description:
Is staying healthy part of serving HaShem? Hilchot Deot 4 sets out the Rambam's regimen: daily exercise, never eating until full, keeping the bowels loose, enough sleep, light foods before heavy ones, avoiding old and processed food, and whether the Rambam kept his own rules.

item.title: Don't Hate in Your Heart: Friends, Love & the Real Misvah of Rebuke | Hilchot Deot Ch. 6
item.description:
Hilchot Deot 6 on friendship and love: we become our company, cleaving to the Sages, loving every Jew who holds the principles of faith and the convert doubly, why hatred in the heart is worse than speaking up, and rebuke as a misvah that works only between friends.

item.title: Lashon Hara: Gossip, Slander & Why Editing the Truth Is Worst | Hilchot Deot Ch. 7
item.description:
Why is editing the truth worse than gossip? The end of Hilchot Deot: rebuking privately and gently, care for orphans, the difference between rekhilut, lashon hara and slander, the root of lashon hara in a bad eye, its dust, and the prohibition of revenge and grudges.
